question: Can shipping Logs v3 avoid decoding a provably rank-dominated disallowed xz sidecar without changing archive bytes, admitted inverse edges, semantics, or failure behavior for allowed gzip/zstd, and with decision-changing create/resource improvement?

mechanism.selector: discover all matches -> choose minimum CODEC_RANK -> product post-filter to allowed_inverse_codecs
mechanism.proposed_rule: Skip a disallowed codec before decode only when its rank is strictly worse than every known allowed codec rank. Better-ranked disallowed codecs remain observable because they can mask a worse-ranked allowed winner under choose-then-filter semantics.

invariants: No benchmark/workload identity in dispatch or admission.
Full-discovery behavior remains the default for research callers when allowed_codecs is omitted.
Shipping valid Logs archive bytes and SHA must be identical to a same-input full-discovery control.
Final admitted inverse-edge targets/sources/codecs must be identical to the same-input full-discovery-then-filter control.
Malformed or oversized disallowed xz must remain ordinary user bytes and must not abort shipping Logs construction.
Malformed supported gzip/zstd remains fail-closed; no parser-error weakening.
Existing archive grammar, reader, recovery, locality/decode ceilings, and release comparators remain unchanged.

product_ab.exact_input: same generated source tree, staged once per paired arm where applicable
product_ab.success: Exactness/semantics gates all green and create/resource evidence is materially favorable enough to justify full external-matrix confirmation.
product_ab.kill: Any byte/SHA/tree/edge semantic change on valid input, any supported-codec failure masking, or no decision-changing create/resource headroom.

claim_boundary: Preregistration only. No product/release credit until exact-head tests plus hosted same-run product A/B and inherited gates pass.
